input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: The guard uses all(...) instead of any(...) over the arguments' help attributes, so the section is gated on every argument being documented rather than on at least one.
- failure path: A command with arguments SRC (help set) and DST (no help) prints no 'Positional arguments' section at all in --help, silently dropping the documented text; conversely a command with zero arguments satisfies all([]) and prints an empty 'Positional arguments' header on every --help.

Reviewer finding
- description: all() over an empty list is True, so a command with no arguments now renders an empty 'Positional arguments' heading.
- rationale: Trigger: any command with no Argument parameters, where format_arguments is called during help generation. args is empty, so all(...) returns True and the section is opened with zero records. The user sees a spurious heading in every such command's --help output.
critique: The finding identifies the same faulty all(...) guard over argument help attributes, and it explains one of the label's failure paths: all([]) being True for zero arguments, which emits an empty heading. It doesn't mention the mixed-help case, but the operation and mechanism are the same as the label's.
